A_general.open_code_note: No public Udemy Business MCP repository or package was found in the prepared repository/package searches. Available evidence describes a hosted server; no public code was available to compare with the deployed endpoint.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Official documentation requires a Udemy Business Enterprise Plan and the AI Connectors add-on. The add-on price is not published on the cited pricing page; it directs customers to contact sales.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Team Plan: $360 per user per year for 2–50 people. Enterprise: contact sales. AI Connectors is a paid Enterprise add-on; its price is not published.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: No per-call MCP price or MCP-specific quota was found. The listed access requirement is a paid Enterprise plan plus the AI Connectors add-on. AI Role Play creation additionally requires the AI Role Play SKU; labs and learning-path search are marked Udemy Business Pro only.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Enterprise plan and AI Connectors add-on required. create_role_play needs an additional AI Role Play SKU; search_labs and search_learning_paths require Udemy Business Pro. Static client credentials are managed in Udemy Business admin settings. Users authenticate and consent. Microsoft Copilot does not currently support creating learning paths.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Udemy controls plan/add-on availability and OAuth; organization admins control static client credentials and internal access to them; users provide sign-in and consent; AI-client capabilities can limit available actions.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with a Bearer challenge pointing to https://api.udemy.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. That metadata identifies https://api.udemy.com as authorization server, header bearer tokens, resource https://api.udemy.com/mcp, scopes course:read, mcp:read, mcp:write, lab:read, offline, and policy/TOS URIs https://www.udemy.com/terms/api/ and https://www.udemy.com/terms/ub/. The authorization-server metadata lists DCR at https://api.udemy.com/auth/external/oidc/dynamic-client/register; grants client_credentials, authorization_code, refresh_token; token auth methods client_secret_post, client_secret_basic, none; PKCE S256; response types token and code; and scopes course:read, lab:read, mcp:read, mcp:write, offline. The base protected-resource URL returned 404. OpenID configuration separately lists authorization_code and refresh_token, PKCE S256, and identity scopes openid, profile:read, email:read, support_context:read, offline_access. Udemy docs also describe static client credentials, redirect/callback URLs, user sign-in and consent. Metadata does not state token lifetime or revocation.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: OAuth bearer access token in Authorization header, as declared in protected-resource metadata.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs identify six retrieval/search tools as read-only and two write tools, create_learning_path and create_role_play. No official tool annotations are published. 2. Docs say client applications, including Claude and ChatGPT, generally prompt for confirmation before writes; no server-enforced confirmation parameter or MCP Elicitation flow is documented. Role-play publication requires later manual admin review. 3. OAuth scopes are course:read, mcp:read, mcp:write, lab:read, offline; docs describe tenant-scoped execution respecting organization licensing/access, user consent, and static credentials managed by admins. DCR and PKCE S256 are advertised. Token lifetime/revocation are not documented. 4. No read-only mode, tool filtering parameter, or environment/region variant found. Product restrictions: labs and learning-path search require Udemy Business Pro; Copilot does not support creating learning paths. 5. Docs say responses contain only discovery metadata; conversations are not passed to MCP, but user-entered data may be sent in tool-call parameters by the AI model. Tenant and licensing scope are documented; field-level masking is not. 6. No MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, result truncation, or per-call costs found. Docs mention client timeouts/token limits and recommend smaller requests. 7. FAQ says server validates tool calls, but schemas and rejection/coercion/correction behavior are not published. No public code. 8. Udemy says operational logs support reliability, security, and abuse detection; log contents/retention/audit access are not specified. 9. Search of the complete official tool list and descriptions found no feedback/rating/report/survey action or documented tool-result upsell. The FAQ has a user feedback section but not an MCP tool. 10. Documentation provides sample system prompts and tool-chaining guidance outside the server; these are not described as enforced server behavior. 11. No documentation found that past agent behavior changes later outputs, tools, resources, or prompts. 12. No nested server or sub-server architecture documented. 13. No raw API, arbitrary query, script, or execution escape-hatch tool appears in the official tool list.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The documented MCP list has no tool to edit an existing Role Play; Udemy says edits must be made manually in instructor tools. create_role_play creates an unpublished shell that requires admin review and manual publication before assignment. search_assessments discovers an assessment but does not enroll or launch it. Microsoft Copilot currently cannot create learning paths. Sources: https://success.udemy.com/s/article/34213384429335?language=en_US

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Udemy recommends a sequence for learning-path creation: search courses, inspect curricula, optionally search labs/assessments, then create. It says agents should gather and confirm role-play details before creation. These are sample-prompt/client recommendations; no server-side enforcement is documented. Exact guidance includes: "Do not include a course without inspecting it first." and "Confirm the scenario summary with the user before creating it".
F_documentation.governance_promises: Udemy states that tool execution is scoped to the customer's tenant and respects organization licensing/access; traffic uses HTTPS/TLS 1.2 or later; discovery requests/responses contain needed metadata and actual conversations are not passed to MCP; operational logs support reliability, security, and abuse detection. Udemy also warns that an external model may send user-provided proprietary data in tool-call parameters and recommends customer policies/guardrails. OAuth consent and admin-managed static credentials are documented.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Udemy describes the connector as real-time discovery from the customer's catalog and content, including custom courses. Created learning paths are private by default. Created Role Plays remain unpublished until an admin reviews and publishes them.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Tenant/licensing scoping, OAuth, and static credential controls are documented as server/account controls. Read-only discovery and private/unpublished defaults are documented outcomes. Confirmation before writes is described as expected client behavior, not a server-enforced control. The system prompt, tool chaining, and recommendation-format instructions are guidance for customer-configured agents. Operational logging is claimed, but details of retention and audit access are not specified.

contradictions: The official support article names 8 tools, while the Claude connector directory and SkillsPlayground list only 5: search_assessments, create_learning_path, and create_role_play are omitted from those catalogue lists. The official list is used.

The OAuth metadata advertises the mcp:write scope and the official tool list documents two write tools, while the FAQ describes app-level client credentials as scoped to specific READ access to content. The docs do not explain how write authorization is represented or separated.

Udemy's FAQ describes tool results as structured, read-only discovery results, while the same official documentation lists create_learning_path and create_role_play as write tools. This appears to describe the discovery-result flow rather than all server operations, but the documentation does not explicitly reconcile the wording.
observations_for_research: The official documentation places agent-side recommendations alongside server feature documentation: sequential tool chaining and user confirmation are recommended in prompts, while only the client is said to request confirmation for writes.
Write tools have distinct lifecycle constraints: learning paths are private by default; role-play scenarios are unpublished and require manual admin review/publication.
The server exposes both static client credentials managed by organization admins and dynamic client registration, with OAuth scopes that include both read and write categories.
